record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can the known inclusion BPL ⊆ CL be extended to the catalytic randomized class CBPL, proving CBPL ⊆ CL?

evidence.quote: The randomized class CBPL was introduced by Datta et al. [DGJ +20]
Problem 20. Extend the BPL ⊆ CL simulation to show CBPL ⊆ CL.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A catalytic Turing machine is a deterministic multitape Turing machine equipped with three tapes: a read-only input tape, a work tape, and an additional catalytic tape. On input x of length n, the work tape has O(log n) cells and the catalytic tape has poly(n) cells. The catalytic tape is initialized with an arbitrary string w of length poly(n), and the machine must produce the correct output for every choice of initial content w, with the additional requirement that, upon halting, the catalytic tape contents are exactly equal to the initial w. The class CL (catalytic logspace) consists of all languages decided by such machines.

A randomized catalytic logspace machine is defined analogously but is additionally given access to a one-way random tape. The class CBPL consists of all languages L for which there exists a randomized catalytic logspace machine M such that for every input x and every initialization w of the catalytic tape:
 (i) Pr[M(x,w) accepts] ≥ 2/3 if x ∈ L, and Pr[M(x,w) accepts] ≤ 1/3 if x ∉ L,
 (ii) with probability 1 the catalytic tape is restored to its initial content w upon halting.

The class BPL is the standard bounded-error randomized logspace class (no catalytic tape), and the inclusion BPL ⊆ CL is known.

Problem. Prove that CBPL ⊆ CL. That is, show that every language decided by a bounded-error randomized catalytic logspace machine can also be decided by a deterministic catalytic logspace machine.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 result (ECCC TR24-106; subsequently appearing in STOC 2025 as "The Structure of Catalytic Space: Capturing Randomness and Time via Compression") establishes unconditionally that CBPL = CL via a "compress-or-compute" framework, thereby giving the desired inclusion CBPL ⊆ CL.

status_evidence.title: ECCC TR24-106: The Structure of Catalytic Space
status_evidence.snippet: CL is equivalent to polytime-bounded, zero-error randomized CL; unconditionally derandomizes catalytic logspace (CBPL = CL).
status_evidence.claim: CBPL = CL is proved unconditionally, so CBPL ⊆ CL holds.

status_evidence.title: The Structure of Catalytic Space: Capturing Randomness and Time via Compression (STOC 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Among the first unconditional derandomization results known for uniform computation; introduces the compress-or-compute algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: The inclusion CBPL ⊆ CL is established unconditionally.
